headline.headline: KNICKS ONE WIN FROM THE PROMISED LAND
headline.deck: New York eyes NBA Finals title as Brunson and Knicks host Spurs in Game 6
headline.body:
NEW YORK -- Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks stand one victory from their first NBA championship in more than five decades, hosting the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night in a Game 6 that the entire basketball world will be watching. The Knicks, seeded third in the Eastern Conference at 53-29, have pushed the second-seeded Spurs to the brink after a series that has turned Madison Square Garden into the loudest building in professional sports.

The Spurs, who went 62-20 during the regular season and entered the playoffs as legitimate title favorites behind Victor Wembanyama, now face elimination on the road. The atmosphere surrounding the series has grown toxic at times -- ESPN anchor Mike Greenberg this week publicly condemned behavior directed at Wembanyama and San Antonio fans in New York, a reminder that the city's passion has curdled into something uglier in recent days.

If the Knicks close it out Friday, it ends a championship drought stretching back to 1973. If Wembanyama and the Spurs force a Game 7, San Antonio returns home with momentum and a building that will be shaking. Tip-off is scheduled for Friday night at the Garden, and the stakes could not be higher.

secondary.headline: TORTORELLA: GOLDEN KNIGHTS NOT FINISHED YET
secondary.deck: Vegas coach vows comeback after Carolina pushes Golden Knights to edge of elimination
secondary.body:
RALEIGH -- John Tortorella has never been a man who accepts a eulogy while still breathing. The Vegas Golden Knights coach made that crystal clear Thursday, insisting that his club is not done despite trailing the Carolina Hurricanes and facing elimination in the Stanley Cup Final. Andrei Svechnikov and the Hurricanes are one win away from hoisting the Cup after a Game 5 victory sent the series back to Vegas with Carolina holding a commanding edge.

Tortorella, who has coached in big moments throughout a career spanning multiple franchises, told reporters that Vegas will force a Game 7 when the series returns to T-Mobile Arena. The Golden Knights will need a performance that matches his confidence -- Carolina has been the sharper team, and the Hurricanes have the crowd momentum heading into what could be a closeout game on the road.

secondary.headline: BICHETTE BOMBS FUEL METS' LATE SQUEEZE PAST CARDINALS
secondary.deck: New York rallies behind four home runs to edge St. Louis 5-4 at Citi Field
secondary.body:
NEW YORK -- Four home runs carried the New York Mets past the St. Louis Cardinals 5-4 on Thursday night at Citi Field, with Bo Bichette's sixth homer of the season joining shots from Alec Burleson, Lars Nootbaar and Crooks in a game that turned on a wild first inning. The Cardinals jumped out to a 1-0 lead before the Mets answered with three runs in the bottom of the first, only to watch St. Louis storm back with three runs in the second to take a 4-3 lead. From that point, both bullpens locked down, and the game settled into a tense pitchers' duel before the Mets scratched across single runs in the fifth and seventh innings to take the lead for good.

The final score of 5-4 required 2 hours and 39 minutes before 37,019 fans who earned every anxious minute. The Cardinals, sitting at 37-29 and second in the NL Central, stranded runners and could not add to their early offensive burst. The Mets, who got no further scoring from either club in the ninth, held on to secure the win and hand St. Louis a defeat the Cardinals would like to forget heading into Friday's series opener against the Minnesota Twins.

secondary.headline: SEAHAWKS' SUPER BOWL LX RINGS TELL A CITY'S STORY
secondary.deck: Seattle received its championship rings Thursday night in a private ceremony celebrating the title
secondary.body:
SEATTLE -- The Seattle Seahawks gathered Thursday night for a private ceremony and received the hardware that will define their franchise for a generation: Super Bowl LX championship rings, set with diamonds and sapphires and designed to honor the fans and the city that backed them through the long road to the title. The rings, revealed at the event, drew immediate praise from players and front office staff who have waited since February's championship victory to hold the finished product in their hands.

For a franchise that won its first Super Bowl after the 2013 season, a second title represents the fulfillment of years of rebuilding. The design choices -- saluting the city and its history -- reflect an organization that understood winning was never just about what happened on the field. Now that the rings are on fingers across the Pacific Northwest, the Seahawks turn their attention to defending the title when the 2026 season begins.

column.headline: THE GARDEN IS GREAT -- BUT NOT LIKE THIS
column.body:
Madison Square Garden is the world's most famous arena, and on a big night it generates a noise and electricity that no other building can match. The Knicks being one game away from their first championship since 1973 is the kind of sports story that deserves to be celebrated loudly and without apology. But what happened outside a New York hotel -- a young man getting pelted, visiting fans harassed -- is not passion. It is ugliness dressed up in blue and orange, and it does not deserve to share a stage with a genuine sports miracle in the making.

Victor Wembanyama came to New York as a competitor, as the face of the franchise trying to stop history from being made at the Garden's expense. He deserved a hostile crowd inside the arena. What he got outside it was something no athlete should experience, and Mike Greenberg was right to say so plainly. The Knicks are on the doorstep of something magnificent. The fans who show up Friday night and make the Garden erupt with legitimate, thunderous basketball noise will be part of that story forever. The ones who turned a city block into something shameful have already written their own ending.

story.headline: TIGERS BLUDGEON TWINS 11-0 AS SIX BOMBERS GO DEEP AT COMERICA
story.deck: Detroit's bats erupt across eight innings to send Minnesota home empty
story.body:
DETROIT — Six different Tigers went deep and winning pitcher K. Montero kept Minnesota off the scoreboard entirely as Detroit hammered the Twins 11-0 Thursday night at Comerica Park before 30,714 fans, turning what looked like a pitching duel into a one-sided demolition by the fourth inning.

Spencer Torkelson led the assault with his 10th home run of the season, joined by Torres, whose pinch-hit blast in the eighth — his fourth of the year — capped a three-run frame that broke the game open for good. Julio Pérez added his seventh, Zach McKinstry his second, and Corey Keith his first career home run as Detroit spread the damage across the fourth, sixth, seventh, and eighth innings. Dingler and McGonigle each contributed doubles. The Twins stranded 11 baserunners, unable to convert any of their opportunities against a Tigers staff that was never seriously threatened.

In New York, the Mets survived a Cardinals comeback to win 5-4, with St. Louis scoring three runs in the second inning to grab a 4-3 lead after the first frame. The Mets answered with single runs in the fifth and seventh — homers from Bichette and Juan Soto, whose 14th blast proved the difference — to hold on in 2:39 before 37,019 at Citi Field. Meanwhile, the Cubs routed Colorado 9-3 behind home runs from Alex Bregman, Seiya Suzuki, and three others, and the Dodgers outlasted Pittsburgh 8-6 in a game marred by two hit batters against Freddie Freeman.

story.headline: EGG ON HIS FACE: WEMBANYAMA PELTED OUTSIDE HOTEL AS KNICKS FANS RUN WILD BEFORE GAME 6
story.deck: Ugly scenes in Manhattan as New York teeters between celebration and embarrassment on Finals eve.
story.body:
NEW YORK -- Victor Wembanyama could not escape the hostility even after the arena lights went dark. The San Antonio Spurs superstar was struck by a thrown egg and showered with boos from a mob of Knicks faithful outside his Midtown Manhattan hotel Thursday night, a scene that drew swift and fierce condemnation from across the sports media landscape. ESPN's Mike Greenberg called the behavior 'an embarrassment to the city and to the sport,' demanding accountability for those who targeted not only Wembanyama but traveling Spurs fans who had done nothing more than wear the wrong colors in the wrong borough.

The ugliness threatens to overshadow what should be a historic moment for New York basketball. The Knicks, carrying a 3-2 series lead into Friday's Game 6 at Madison Square Garden, stand one win away from their first NBA championship in more than half a century. Jalen Brunson has been the heartbeat of this run, willing a 53-29 regular-season squad past every expectation and now to the doorstep of glory against a San Antonio team that won 62 games and entered the postseason as the league's most feared outfit. The contrast is stark -- the Spurs were the class of the Western Conference all season, and Wembanyama has been otherworldly throughout, yet New York has found a way to claw to the brink.

League officials confirmed Thursday they are reviewing the hotel incident and working with New York Police Department representatives to identify those responsible for throwing the egg. A first defendant in a related atmosphere of athlete-targeting crimes -- the 2024 string of burglaries at the homes of high-profile players -- was separately sentenced Friday to 24 months in federal prison, a grim backdrop to a Finals that has grown increasingly charged. Tip-off for Game 6 is set for 8 p.m. Eastern at the Garden, where Brunson and the Knicks will attempt to silence every distraction and finish the job.

story.headline: SVECHNIKOV, HURRICANES PUT GOLDEN KNIGHTS ON THE BRINK
story.deck: Carolina one win from Stanley Cup after dominant Game 5 victory in Raleigh
story.body:
RALEIGH, N.C. -- Andrei Svechnikov scored twice and Sebastian Aho added a second-period goal as the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the Vegas Golden Knights 4-2 in Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final on Thursday night, pushing the series to 3-2 and leaving Carolina one victory away from its first championship.

The Hurricanes' top line finally delivered when it mattered most, with Svechnikov's brace giving Carolina the cushion it needed to withstand Vegas. The Golden Knights, who have now dropped two straight games in the series, trailed 4-2 heading into the final period and could not mount a comeback. The loss sends Vegas home facing potential elimination in Game 6.

Golden Knights coach John Tortorella, never short on defiance, told reporters after the game that his team is far from finished. 'We're not done yet,' Tortorella vowed, promising the series would return to Raleigh for a Game 7. Carolina, however, will carry all the momentum into Vegas when Game 6 drops the puck, with the Hurricanes needing just one more win to hoist the Stanley Cup.

story.headline: SHEDEUR SANDERS FINDS HIS FOOTING IN CLEVELAND AS BROWNS BET BIG ON FRANCHISE REVIVAL
story.deck: Cleveland's prized rookie quarterback begins reshaping a franchise starved for stability.
story.body:
CLEVELAND — Shedeur Sanders arrived at the Browns facility Monday for the start of organized team activities carrying the weight of a franchise on his shoulders and, by all accounts, looking comfortable doing it. The former Colorado star, selected by Cleveland in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft, has wasted no time impressing new offensive coordinator Tommy Rees with his command of the huddle, his quick release, and the same poise under pressure that made him one of the most scrutinized prospects in recent memory.

General manager Andrew Berry moved aggressively this offseason to surround Sanders with weapons, signing veteran wide receiver Tyler Lockett to a two-year deal after his release from Seattle and trading a third-round pick to Jacksonville for tight end Evan Engram. The additions give Sanders proven targets who know how to run crisp routes in a West Coast system. Head coach Kevin Stefanski, entering a critical contract year himself, has publicly staked his offensive identity on the young quarterback's development.

Around the league, the offseason reshaped several other rosters in dramatic fashion. The Dallas Cowboys parted ways with Dak Prescott after 10 seasons, releasing the veteran signal-caller in a salary cap move that stunned the NFL world and immediately sparked speculation about his next destination. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders agreed to terms with linebacker Roquan Smith on a surprise homecoming deal, and the Philadelphia Eagles locked up receiver A.J. Brown through 2029 before he could test free agency.
